definitions.gloss: metallurgy; metalworking; the science and technology of metals
definitions.explanation: The broad field encompassing the extraction of metals from ores, refining, alloying, shaping, and studying the properties of metals and alloys. An academic and industrial term.

examples.japanese: {冶金|やきん}⟦{学|がく}→〜学：09846_gaku⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{学|まな}ぶ→学ぶ：01987_manabu⟧。
{冶金|やきん}⟦{技術|ぎじゅつ}→技術：01389_gijutsu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{発展|はってん}→発展：03561_hatten⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{文明|ぶんめい}→文明：03611_bunmei⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{変|か}えた→変える：01089_kaeru⟧。
⟦{日本|にほん}→日本：03876_nihon⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{冶金|やきん}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{刀剣|とうけん}→刀剣：23020_touken⟧{作|づく}り⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{伝統|でんとう}→伝統：09585_dentou⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{根|ね}ざしている→根ざす：13125_nezasu⟧。

notes:
Composed of {冶|や} (smelt, cast) and {金|きん} (metal). The character {冶|や} specifically refers to the heating and working of metals, giving the compound its specialized meaning.

Metallurgy has deep historical roots in Japan, particularly through {刀鍛冶|かたなかじ} (swordsmithing) and {鋳物|いもの} (casting) traditions. The academic discipline is studied in university engineering departments, often under names like {冶金|やきん}⟦{工学|こうがく}→工学：04862_kougaku⟧ (metallurgical engineering) or the more modern ⟦{材料|ざいりょう}→材料：02831_zairyou⟧⟦{工学|こうがく}→工学：04862_kougaku⟧ (materials engineering).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {冶金|やきん}⟦{学|がく}→〜学：09846_gaku⟧: metallurgy (as an academic discipline)
- {冶金|やきん}⟦{工学|こうがく}→工学：04862_kougaku⟧: metallurgical engineering
- ⟦{粉末|ふんまつ}→粉末：13772_funmatsu⟧{冶金|やきん}: powder metallurgy
- {冶金|やきん}⟦{技術|ぎじゅつ}→技術：01389_gijutsu⟧: metallurgical technology

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{製錬|せいれん}→製錬：24155_seiren⟧: smelting — the specific process of extracting metal from ore, a subset of metallurgy
- {鍛冶|かじ}: blacksmithing, forging — the traditional craft of shaping heated metal, a more hands-on term
- ⟦{合金|ごうきん}→合金：17137_goukin⟧: alloy — a product of metallurgy, not the field itself
